<p class="has-text-align-center wp-block-paragraph" style="font-size:26px"><strong>Intro</strong></p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><span style="font-weight: bold; text-decoration: underline;">Audience</span><b>:</b> Experienced Cryptographers seeking a no-fluff primer on LP.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><strong><span style="text-decoration: underline;">Goal</span>:</strong> Rapid familiarization with the structure and framework of LP, as well as current challenges, hypotheses, and methods of attack.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><span style="text-decoration: underline;"><strong>Background</strong></span><strong>:</strong> LP is broadly considered the most difficult puzzle of the digital age, and has gone unsolved for <a href="https://www.cicadasolvers.com/timelines/" data-type="page" data-id="500" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">over a decade</a>. <p class="wp-block-paragraph"><strong><span style="text-decoration: underline;">Language</span></strong>: <br>Runeglish (Rune-English derived from the <a href="https://www.cicadasolvers.com/wiki/gematria-primus/" data-type="page" data-id="217" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Gematria Primus</a>)</p>

<p class="has-text-align-center wp-block-paragraph" style="font-size:26px"><strong>Structural Overview</strong></p>



<details class="wp-block-details is-layout-flow wp-block-details-is-layout-flow"><summary>Pagination</summary>
<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><a href="https://www.cicadasolvers.com/lp2/" data-type="page" data-id="276" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">LP2</a>‘s 58 pages all have numerical names, as defined by 3301 in their May 2014 file dump. The names of the pages are consecutive whole numbers, i.e. ‘0.jpg,1.jpg,2.jpg…57.jpg’. This is a departure from the nomenclature of LP1.</p>
</details>



<details class="wp-block-details is-layout-flow wp-block-details-is-layout-flow"><summary>Segmentation</summary>
<p class="wp-block-paragraph">LP2 consists of multiple ‘sections’, easily recognized by <a href="https://www.cicadasolvers.com/wiki/marginalia/" data-type="page" data-id="242" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">marginalia</a> and <a href="https://www.cicadasolvers.com/wiki/rubrication/" data-type="page" data-id="244" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">rubricated</a> <a href="https://www.cicadasolvers.com/wiki/incipit/" data-type="page" data-id="246" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">incipits</a>. Stylistically reminiscent of <a href="https://www.cicadasolvers.com/wiki/illuminated-manuscript/" data-type="page" data-id="248" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">illuminated manuscripts</a>.</p>
</details>



<details class="wp-block-details is-layout-flow wp-block-details-is-layout-flow"><summary>Delimiters</summary>
<p class="wp-block-paragraph">1:1 delimiter congruency is assumed to be maintained, as it is in LP1 and the two solved pages of LP2. Liber Primus has unique delimiters used for spaces, line breaks, paragraph, section end, etc. The dot delimiters also correspond to the ASCII control characters LF (Line Feed), CR (Carriage Return), and ETB (End of Transmission Block)</p>
</details>



<details class="wp-block-details is-layout-flow wp-block-details-is-layout-flow"><summary>GP Values</summary>
<p class="wp-block-paragraph">GP letter values can be used to construct prime words, phrases, and sentences/lines. Prime/emirp GP sums serve an important role as exemplified by <a href="https://www.cicadasolvers.com/57-jpg/" data-type="page" data-id="285" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">57.jpg</a></p>
</details>



<details class="wp-block-details is-layout-flow wp-block-details-is-layout-flow"><summary>Artwork</summary>
<p class="wp-block-paragraph">LP contains various forms of both original and existing artwork. 1033.jpg, sometimes called the ‘<a href="https://www.cicadasolvers.com/wiki/cover/" data-type="page" data-id="220" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">cover</a>‘ of LP, is a collage of four William Blake pieces: <a href="https://www.cicadasolvers.com/wiki/newton/" data-type="page" data-id="231" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Newton</a>, <a href="https://www.cicadasolvers.com/wiki/the-ancient-of-days/" data-type="page" data-id="237" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">The Ancient of Days</a>, and two versions of <a href="https://www.cicadasolvers.com/wiki/nebuchadnezzar/" data-type="page" data-id="234" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Nebuchadnezzar</a><a href="https://www.cicadasolvers.com/nebuchadnezzar/" data-type="page" data-id="234" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">.</a> Within LP2, ‘sections’ are ostensibly indicated by original marginalia. Specific pages also contain separate, page-relevant original artwork — such as cuneiform numerals or mobius strips. Additionally, several instances of edited artwork from known sources exist — such as the mayfly and oak tree.</p>
</details>

<details class="wp-block-details is-layout-flow wp-block-details-is-layout-flow"><summary>Single-rune words</summary>
<p class="wp-block-paragraph">In both LP1 and LP2, we see many single-rune words. Ostensibly, these can only be “A” or “I”. A third, less likely possibility also exists: “O”, used as an interjection/exclamation. William Blake, often referenced throughout the Cicada 3301 puzzles, often used “O” in this manner. When applying the Gematria Primus, it becomes apparent that single runes can be translated into two or three letter digraphs/diphthongs such as “TH”, “EO”, “NG/ING”, “OE”, “AE”, “IA/IO”, and “EA”. These additional characters make cribbing much more difficult due to the increase in possibilities that we have to work through.</p>
</details>



<details class="wp-block-details is-layout-flow wp-block-details-is-layout-flow"><summary>Dis Legomenon</summary>
<p class="wp-block-paragraph">The 6-gram DJUBEI <a href="https://www.cicadasolvers.com/wiki/dis-legomenon/" data-type="page" data-id="266" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">occurs twice</a> in the corpus of unsolved LP pages, marking the longest such repetition and a possible point of attack.</p>
</details>



<details class="wp-block-details is-layout-flow wp-block-details-is-layout-flow"><summary>Character Interchangeability</summary>
<p class="wp-block-paragraph">There is strong evidence to support the encryption was performed on the runes instead of the latin characters.  This is due to not being able to go back and forth between runes and latin characters.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">An example would be: ᛏᚻᚫᛡ -> THAEIO -> ᚦᚫᛡ</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">There is more information <a href="https://www.cicadasolvers.com/thoughts-on-runes/" data-type="page" data-id="297">here</a>.</p>
</details>

<details class="wp-block-details is-layout-flow wp-block-details-is-layout-flow"><summary>Analysis of Recent Communications</summary>
<p class="wp-block-paragraph">28th July 2015: Planned Parenthood message. The GP sum of the entire message is 11,570 = 2 × 5 × 13 × 89, four of the first five Fib primes. Also there is the 5-3-2-5-7 spacing or some-such. Possibly the Fib and Prime sequences slightly overlaid, and going in opposite directions? Or two Prime sequences? </p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">6th Jan 2016: LP Is The Way message where the Fibonacci sequence was subtracted cumulatively from 464 (3301’s prime index) and the resultant number was used as a prime index to convert it into a prime (Emphasis on the sequence.) There are other ways to interpret the precise algorithm at use here, frustratingly. On the flip side, there are some interpretations that are very similar to the one used in 15.jpg. </p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">29th April 2017: Beware False Paths message — the GP sum of this message is the next term the algorithm found in the 2016 message, IMO confirming that what was found in the 2016 message is not a coincidence. </p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">To summarise: 3301 like meshing the Prime and Fibonacci sequences together in various ways, so I think it’s definitely worth exploring the Prime-Fibonacci space.</p>

<p class="wp-block-paragraph">56.jpg was ‘solved’ days-weeks after its release via the following method:</p>



<pre class="wp-block-preformatted">Subtract prime numbers - 1 in order:<br>decimal[i] = (decimal[i] - (primes[i] - 1)) % 29<br><br>i.e.<br>decimal[0] = (decimal[0] - (2 - 1)) % 29<br>decimal[1] = (decimal[1] - (3 - 1)) % 29<br>decimal[2] = (decimal[2] - (5 - 1)) % 29<br>decimal[3] = (decimal[3] - (7 - 1)) % 29<br>decimal[4] = (decimal[4] - (11 - 1)) % 29<br><br>Note that φ(p) = p - 1, where p is prime and φ is <a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Euler%27s_totient_function" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Euler's totient function</a></pre>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Here is the deciphered text:</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><em>WITHIN THE DEEP WEB, THERE EXISTS A PAGE THAT HASHES TO</em></p>



<pre class="wp-block-preformatted"><strong>36367763ab73783c7af284446c<br><br>59466b4cd653239a311cb7116<br><br>d4618dee09a8425893dc7500b<br><br>464fdaf1672d7bef5e891c6e227<br><br>4568926a49fb4f45132c2a8b4</strong></pre>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><em>IT IS THE DUTY OF EVERY PILGRIM TO SEEK OUT THIS PAGE</em></p>
